title: Density token mapping and sticky filter bar for virtualized tables
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Current table components have multiple ad-hoc density values (tight/compact/default/comfortable) implemented in components, CSS utilities, and a couple of JS-level layout heuristics. This has led to inconsistent row heights and spacing across table variants (standard table, virtualized list, row-stacked mobile fallback) and brittle visual regressions when theme tokens are updated. Additionally, the sticky filter / sort bar for long datasets behaves inconsistently with virtualization: filters detach visually when rows are recycled or when the header is scrolled outside the virtualization window. This ticket defines a design-led migration to a single density token surface, a mapping strategy for existing components, and a microinteraction pattern for a sticky filter bar that plays nicely with virtualized rendering and keyboard/assistive tech.
acceptance_criteria: A density token spec (CSS token names + semantic values) exists and maps to all table variants (standard/virtualized/mobile/compact) in the design system
Design tokens documented in Figma and Confluence with code-ready token names matching the implementation (e.g., token.table.rowHeight.compact -> 32px)
Prototype of sticky filter bar shows stable attachment to the visual viewport independent of virtualization window; no visual jitter when rows recycle
Keyboard focus and screen reader announcements work when the sticky filter becomes pinned/unpinned (ARIA roles and live region text defined)
Engineering has an implementation plan with a migration path for 3 major repos and a toggle for old/new token behavior for canary rollout
Visual QA checklist and screenshots for default/compact/comfortable densities across breakpoints included in Confluence
engineering_notes: Engineering owners: @lina-chen (frontend) and @marcus-garcia (runtime). Need to coordinate with infra for virtualization window change events.
Suggested implementation: expose token API (CSS vars) and a small runtime shim that maps token sets to virtualization cell height; allow optional per-table override via data-density attribute.
Performance risk: introducing a live sticky element reading virtualization offsets could cause reflow if not throttled. Propose IntersectionObserver + transform-based pinning.
Migration plan: 1) Add token definitions and variable fallbacks; 2) Add small feature-flagged shim used by Console canary; 3) Run visual diff on key dashboards; 4) Flip default after 2 cycles
decisions: Canonical density is semantic (compact / default / comfortable) and maps to token sets, not pixel values embedded in components
Sticky filter bar will use transform-based pinning and a live region with a single short announcement: 'Filter bar pinned' / 'Filter bar unpinned'
Row height token names will be prefixed with token.table.rowHeight.* to keep token discovery straightforward
Default keyboard shortcut for focusing the filter input will be preserved; when sticky, focus moves to the pinned element without changing tab order
